messages.subject: help with model
parts:
Hi,
Very new to use using STAN. I have the model below. If I change the beta[m]~ normal(0,sigma_b_s) ; to beta[m]~ normal(0,10) ; it works fine.
I am getting a error with 

Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

The short term end point is to expand the model on eta_b_s[m] ~ normal(0,10); to eta_b_s[m] ~ normal( a + bx ,s_eta); to model the variance of the regression coefficients.

It would be great to have some help to understand why I am getting this error. 

BW,
Inti

data {
    int<lower=0> N; // number of samples
    int<lower=0> M; // number of predictors
    matrix[N,M] x;  // predictors
    vector[N] y; // outcomes
}
parameters { 
    real sigma; // error observations
    vector[M] beta; // predictor effects 
    real alpha; // intercept
}


model {    
    vector<lower=0, upper=100>[M] sigma_b_s;
    vector[M] eta_b_s;
    alpha ~ normal(0,100);
    sigma ~ cauchy(0,5);

    for (m in 1:M){
        eta_b_s[m] ~ normal(0,10);
        sigma_b_s ~ exponential(eta_b_s[m]);
        beta[m]~ normal(0,sigma_b_s) ;
    }
    for (n in 1:N)
        y[n] ~ normal(alpha + x[n] * beta, sigma);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] help with model
parts:
The variables you define locally in the model need to be
defined as parameters:

Unlike in BUGS, Stan variables must be defined before
they are used. Data and transformed data is defined as
data is read in. Parameters are defined externally and
transformed parameters must be defined in their block.
Local variables must be defined with "<-" before they are
used in a block.

Your problem is with local variables, which must be defined
before they are used. The sampling statement "~" doesn't
literally do sampling --- it just increments the log
probability function.

- Bob
